id.description: The event's own id. Stable across a retry of the same event.

ts.description: When it happened, by Chips' clock. Stamped on the way in; a value the sender writes is replaced.

workspace_id.description: A workspace identifier: `ws_` followed by a ULID.

space_id.description: The space, when the event belongs to one.

run_id.description: The run, when the event belongs to one.

seq.description: Assigned by the server on append, monotonic per workspace. Absent on the way in.

idempotency_key.description: Required on every client-originated write. Sending the same key twice is a no-op.

kind.description: Whether a person, a harness, one of a harness's agents or Chips itself acted.

id.description: The participant id, or `system` for Chips.

harness_id.description: For an agent: the harness it speaks through, whose budget and runs are the agent's (ADR 0087). Filled in by Chips.

actor.description: The participant an event is attributed to.

approval_id.description: Minted by the harness, so a retry after a reconnect is the same ask.

step_id.description: The plan step this ask belongs to.

kind.description: A dotted verb, for example `email.send` or `payment.transfer`. Policy rules glob on it.

input.description: The arguments, shaped by the tool being called.

external.description: True when the action leaves the workspace.

irreversible.description: True when the action cannot be undone.

money_usd.description: Amount at stake, in US dollars.

action.description: An action a harness proposes to take.

question.description: The question the person answers yes or no, as one sentence in plain words: `Turn off the Robinhood connector?`. The card leads with it. Without it the card is headed by the preview's title, else the action's kind (ADR 0142).

effect.description: What a yes does, in a sentence or two: `Its 73 tools disappear from every Space.` Drawn under the question.

lasts.description: How long a yes keeps working: `once` for this action alone, `standing` for a grant that holds until it is taken back, such as a folder an agent may keep working in. The card says which.

preview.description: What the approver sees. Omit only when the action speaks for itself.

items.description: A risk class the policy engine can match a rule against.

risk.description: Risk classes. The policy engine matches rules against these.

sources.description: Where the harness got what it is about to act on.

kind.description: Whether the source is outside the workspace.

label.description: What to show in the receipt, for example `vendor website`.

url.description: Where to look, when there is somewhere to look.

items.description: A source a harness used, shown in the receipt and on approval cards.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the approval expires. Every approval has an expiry and a fallback.

fallback.description: What happens on expiry. Denying is the default, and the safe one.

approvers.description: Who may answer, as the harness asks it: `owner`, `any` (the room, but its guests), `role:<name>` (a standing in the space or in the workspace), or a person id. `lead` (the lane's lead, when the run is a lane's) is a policy rule's to name, never a harness's, and never for an ask that matters — money, a deletion, an external action reach a person. Chips resolves them — policy's own list when a rule names one — to ids before the event is stored, and only those may decide it; a person may hand it on with `approval.routed`.

items.description: `owner`, `any`, `lead`, `role:<name>`, or a specific person id; a lead harness's id once resolved.

editable.description: Whether the approver may change the input before allowing.

resume_token.description: Lets a paused command-line run continue hours later. Approvals outlive processes.

description: The thing a group chat cannot do: an action, a preview, a risk class, who may answer, and an audit record.
title: ApprovalRequest
